correctness.rationale: With weights \(w_k=|k|+2\), nearest-neighbor conductances are exactly one and detailed balance gives \(\pi(k)=w_k/(L^2+5L+2)\). Jacobi Sturm oscillation and reflection imply the first excited mode is odd for every L. The half-interval Rayleigh quotient is exact. The mass quadrature is \(b_h=b_0+h b_1+O(h^2a)\) uniformly on all piecewise-linear zero-origin trials. Simple-eigenvalue perturbation of \(-u''=\nu(h)(x+2h)u\) with \(u(0)=0\) and \(u'(1)=\nu(h)hu(1)/2\) and Galerkin error O(h²) gives \(\lambda_L=\mu L^{-3}-cL^{-4}+O(L^{-5})\). Airy root condition fixes µ and the positive integral formula fixes c. Detailed-balance, parity and sampled asymptotic numerical checks (2953 assertions) corroborate but are not a proof of the infinite limit.

value.rationale: Finite reflecting confinement is a natural regularization of a genuinely subdiffusive random walk with position-dependent waiting rates. The theorem computes its exact leading equilibration timescale and a nonzero order-\(L^{-4}\) microscopic correction, which resolves separate endpoint quadrature and lattice holding-weight effects. These observables go beyond the established infinite-line spreading exponent and allow quantitative finite-trap relaxation predictions; neither a routine stationary normalization nor a computation at one arbitrary chain size.
